 J U D G M E N T

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .35,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sri.Janardhan @ Janardhan Reddy,
S/o.Ramesh, in a road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 21.09.2022 at about 06.45 a.m., when deceased Sri.Janardhan @ Janardhan Reddy was working in front of Harshith Hotel, the driver of Maxi Cab bearing Regn.No.KA-51-AB-8488, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner while taking the vehicle reverse and dashed against the deceased resulting in accident.
Due to said accident, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter, he was shifted to Sapthagiri Hospital, Bengaluru and then shifted to K.C.General Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 21.09.2022 to 23.09.2022 and later shifted to Rajalakshmi Hospital and Research Center, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 23.09.2022 to 11.10.2022 for about 19 days and undergone surgeries and discharged with an advice to take follow-up treatment.

entities.text: Rajalakshmi Hospital and Research Center, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: After few months, the deceased leg got infected at operated site and not recovered.
In spite of best efforts by the doctors, the deceased died due to accidental injuries on 20.08.2023.

Thereafter postmortem was conducted at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and body was handed over to petitioners and shifted the body to their native place and spent a sum of .4,50,000/- towards medicine, transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was working as Labour and earning a sum of .18,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners lost bread earning member of the family and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Maxi cab by its driver.
The respondent No.1 & 2, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

sentences.text: In pursuance of notice, the respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal through his counsel and filed his written statement.
Though respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through his counsel, he has not filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.1 denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.1 also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as place, time and manner of accident.
The respondent No.1 contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further respondent No.1 admitted the aspect of issue of policy of insurance in favour of 2 nd respondent pertaining to Maxi cab and contended that the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the insured vehicle had no permit and FC as on the date of alleged accident.
Further contended that the deceased was not died due to the accidental injuries.
Further on the date of accident, the maxi cab was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of driver of maxi cab.

Further contended that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of deceased, who without having proper looks out vehicular movements of road and without noticing on coming vehicles was standing in the middle of the road and caused the accident, as such the accident took place due to negligence on the part of deceased and not due to negligence on the part of driver of maxi cab, as such petition is to be rejected for want of negligence on the part of driver of maxi cab.
The amount claimed by petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioners prove that the husband of petitioner No.1(a) and father of petitioner No.1(b & c) namely Sri.Janardhan @ Janardhan Reddy succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 21.09.2022 at about 06.45 a.m.,
while he was working in front of Harshith Hotel, Pipe Line Road, Prashanth Nagar,
T.Dasarahalli, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of Maxi Cab bearing Regn.No.KA-51-AB-8488 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to substantiate the contention of the petition, the Petitioner No.1/wife of deceased got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.21 and closed evidence of petitioner side.
On the other hand, the respondent insurance got examined its Area Manager Legal-Claims as RW.1 and got marked document at Ex.R.1 and closed evidence of their side.

7. Heard arguments on both side and perused the materials available on records.

sentences.text: This Tribunal answers the above issues as below:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioners that deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 21.09.2022 at about 06.45 a.m., while he was working in front of Harshith Hotel, Pipe Line Road,
Prashanth Nagar, T.Dasarahalli, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of Maxi Cab bearing Regn.No.KA-51-AB-8488 by its driver.
10. The Petitioner No.1/wife of deceased Sri. Shruthi Divate got examined as PW.1.
In the chief- examination, Pw-1 deposed that her husband was died due to the rash and negligent driving of Maxi Cab by its driver.

In order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of Maxi Cab, the petitioners produced Ex.P.2 First Information statement lodged by deceased petitioner i.e,
Sri.Janardhan Reddy S/o.Ramesh with police on 21.09.2022.
On the basis of first information lodged by the deceased, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC.
In first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the Maxi Cab.
The FIR is registered against the driver of offending vehicle and same does not appear to have been questioned or challenged.
The petitioners furnished the mahazar which is marked as Ex.P.3.
The said document discloses the aspect of police visiting the place of accident after registration of FIR and the place of accident has been described in the said document.
In the said document also, the accident is stated to haven caused due to negligence on the part of driver of maxi cab.
Further, the petitioner furnished the Wound certificate which is marked as Ex.P.5 and said document discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.
Further, the petitioner furnished the Discharge summaries which are marked as Ex.P.6 and 7.
The said documents disclose the aspect of injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.
The Petitioner has taken treatment at K.C.General Hospital from 21.09.2022 to 23.09.2022 and at Rajalakshmi Hospital and Research Center hospital from 23.09.2022 to 11.10.2022.

11. On the other hand, the respondent insurance got examined its Area Manager Legal- Claims as RW.1 and got marked document at Ex.R.1.
The evidence of Rw-1 is not of much consequence to the respondents in order to disprove the contention of petitioners.

PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to dispute or controvert the contention of petitioners related to cause of accident and negligence of driver of offending vehicle, could be elicited.
12. The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by the petitioners are to be looked into in order to ascertain the aspect of negligence.
The materials placed before the Tribunal points towards the negligence on the part of driver of offending maxi cab in the cause of accident.
So, the oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioners discloses that the accident was caused due to rash and negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of petitioners coupled with the documents produced before this tribunal, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of maxi cab bearing Regn.No.KA-51-AB-8488 by its driver and deceased succumbed to injuries.

Accordingly,
Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.

13. Issue No.2:- During the pendency of petition, the petitioner by name late Sri.Janardhan @
Janardhan Reddy, S/o.Ramesh died and his Lrs were brought on record Smt.Shruthi Divate,
W/o.
Late Janardhan @ Janardhan Reddy examined as PW.1.
In the chief examination, Pw-1 deposed that her husband was taking treatment and she has spent more than .3,50,000/- towards medical treatment, transportation of body, funeral and obsequies ceremony.
Further in her chief examination, she has deposed that due to death of her husband, they have lost love and affection and they lost future support.

14. This court rely upon the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court decided on 16.08.2021 in Civil Appeal No.4800 of 2021 between The Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Kahlon @ Jasmail Singh Kahlon (deceased) through his Legal Representative Narinder Kahlon Gosakan and Another.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court at Para No.18 held as follows:
"The Tribunal, on technicalities rejected his claim for salary, medical expenses and percentage of disability and granted a measly compensation of Rupees one lakh only by a cryptic order.

We are, therefore, of the opinion that while the claim for personal injuries may not have survived after the death of the injured unrelated to the accident or injuries, during the pendency of the appeal, but the claims for loss of estate caused was available to and could be pursued by the legal representatives of the deceased in the appeal."

sentences.text: With due respect to the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, the ratio laid down in the above judgments is applicable to the case on hand.
15. The petitioners contended that the husband of petitioner No.1(a) by name Janardhan @
Janardhan
Reddy died due to the injuries caused in consequences of the accident.
The accident occurred on 21.09.2022 and the petitioner died on 20.08.2023.
The petitioners furnished the wound certificate, which is marked as Ex.P.5, wherein the deceased is stated to have sustained injury to the ankle, right and left lower leg.
The said aspect could be noticed in the discharge summaries also.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of deceased sustaining injuries to the leg due to the accident.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to rebut or disprove the aspect of injury sustained by the deceased.
No materials are placed to show that the injuries sustained by deceased were not due to accident.
The petitioners also furnished the postmortem report, which is marked as Ex.P.13.
As per Ex.P.13, the postmortem of body of deceased is conducted by the doctor at Victoria Hospital and after examination of body of deceased, detailed report is given as per Ex.P.13.
In Ex.P13, the deceased is stated to have died due to Septicemia as a result of infection of right leg.
It is pertinent to note that the cause of death is stated to be result of infection of right leg which appears to be the part of the body which got injured in the accident.
The postmortem report indicates the aspect of infection being caused to the injured part of the body and the said infection is stated to be the cause for the death of Janardhan @ Janardhan Reddy.

16. The counsel for respondent No.1 contended that the petitioner No.1(a) as well as the relatives of the deceased gave statement before the police at the time of inquest stating that the deceased was alcoholic and not used to eat properly and take care of his health and that resulted in the death of deceased.

Though the statement of relatives and wife of deceased indicates that the deceased was consuming alcohol and not looking after his health properly, no satisfactory materials are placed to show that the said aspects resulted in the death of Janardhan @ Janardhan Reddy.
The post mortem report reveals the aspect of infection being caused to the leg and said infection is the cause for the death of Janardhan.

Though the respondent No.1 raised the contention regarding the consuming of alcohol and not looking after the health by the deceased, the materials on record do not are not sufficient and satisfactory to substantiate the said contention.
The statement of wife and relatives of deceased cannot be considered as sufficient proof to ascertain the cause of death.
The PM Report placed before the tribunal does not disclose the aspect of presence of traces of alcohol in the body.
In PM report, it clearly stated that the cause of death is due to infection of right leg, which is the injured part of the deceased.
The cause of death is mentioned in the post mortem report after detailed analysis of the body and the cause of death is mentioned as septicemia.
The materials on record disclose that the deceased sustained injury to the leg and the PM report indicates the aspect of infection being caused to right leg which is got injured in the accident.
As such, as per the PM Report, the cause of death appears to be due to infection of right leg and not due to the reasons stated by wife and relatives of deceased in their statement before the police.

The report as per Ex.P13, is arrived after examination and analysis of parts of the body in accordance with scientific methods and said results prevail over the statement given by wife and relatives of deceased. Post mortem is the authenticated document for ascertaining the cause of death.

The cause of death can be ascertained by examination and analysis of the body in accordance with scientific method and the report submitted by doctor by adopting said methods appears sufficient for ascertaining the cause of Janardhan Alias Janardhan Reddy vs Liberty General Insurance Co. sentences.text: The PM report discloses the actual cause of death of Janardhan @ Janardhan Reddy and the same is due to infection of right leg.

Though the death is caused after lapse of more than 10 months,
Ex.P.13 clearly indicates the aspect of infection being caused to the injured.
The materials on record disclose the nexus between the accidental injuries and the cause of death due to accidental injuries.
The materials on record disclose that the cause of death of Janardhan is due to accidental injuries.

On consideration of materials on record, it can be duly construed that deceased Janardhan @
Janardhan Reddy died due to Septicemia i.e., infection to right leg which is the consequence of accidental injuries.
The respondents not furnished satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the document furnished by petitioners related to cause of death of Janardhan.

17. The petitioners succeeded in establishing that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-51-AB- 8488 by its driver and that Janardhan died due to the injuries caused in the accident.
As Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative and as the cause of death is due to the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

The Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc., in order to assess the compensation.

(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings:
(i) In the petition, the age of the deceased Sri.Janardhan @ Janardhan Reddy S/o.Ramesh is shown as 44 years.
In order to prove the age of deceased, the petitioners produced Ex.P.21 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card of deceased, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 16.10.1980.
The accident occurred on 21.09.2022.
As per the said document, the age of the deceased appears to be 42 years.
The respondents not placed any satisfactory materials in order to disprove the age of deceased.
No materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to disprove or rebut the document furnished by petitioners related to age of deceased.
In the absence of rebuttal material, the document furnished by petitioners is to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
The materials on record disclose the age of deceased to be 42 years as on the date of accident and as such, same is taken into consideration.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Smt. Sarla Verma case the multiplier applicable in present case is '14'.
( ii )
The petitioners contended that deceased Sri.Janardhan @ Janardhan Reddy was working as Labour at Harshith Hotel and earning a sum of .18,000/- per month.
In order to substantiate the said aspect, the petitioners not produced any documents.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the court to show the occupation and income of deceased.
The petitioners not furnished any materials to show that the deceased was earning .18,000/- per month, as contended by them.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income of deceased is to be taken into consideration.
As no satisfactory materials are placed by petitioner related to income of deceased, as per their contention, the notional income is to be considered.
On perusal of the materials on record, the notional income is considered as .15,500/- per month.

sentences.text: In Hem Raj V/s the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of a case.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Both the situations stand at the same footing.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble supreme court of India, the petitioners entitled for future prospects.

In National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi and others, the Hon'be Supreme Court held that, in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 25% of the established income should be warranted where the deceased was aged between 40 to 50 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd V/s Pranaya Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand deceased was aged about 42 years.
Hence, in view of ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners are entitled for additional 25% to the established income.
The established income of the deceased was .15,500/- and 25% of .15,500/- is .3,875/-.
So, the total gross income of deceased was .15,500/- + .3,875/- = .19,375/- per month.
The deceased Sri.Janardhan @ Janardhan @ Janardhan Reddy is married and died leaving behind wife and children.
In order to prove the same, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.21 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Cards of wife and children of deceased.

On perusal of the said document,
it reveals that petitioner No.1(a) is the wife and petitioner No.1(b) & 1(c) are the children of deceased.
The respondents not furnished any materials to doubt or dispute the relationship of petitioners with that of deceased.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal to rebut the document furnished by petitioners to prove the aspect of relationship with the deceased.
The materials placed before the Tribunal disclose that petitioner No.1(a) is the wife and petitioner No.1(b) & 1(c) are the children of deceased.
On perusal of the same, it reveals that petitioners No.1(a) to 1(c) are the wife and children of deceased respectively.

Hence, petitioner No.1(a) to 1(c)
are considered as dependents on the income of deceased.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Smt.Sarla Verma case, where number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd has to be deducted from the gross income of deceased towards his personal expenses and remaining is to be taken as dependency.

Thus, petitioners are entitled to compensation of .21,69,888/- towards loss of dependency which is calculated as follows:

1/3rd of .19,375/- .12,916/-
 (deduction of  .6,459/-)
.12,916/- multiply by .1,54,992/- 12 .1,54,992/- multiply .21,69,888/- by 14 Multiplier (B)
Towards Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses; In the present case, the date of accident is 21.09.2022.

In view of ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Pranay Sethi case, the petitioners are entitled for additional 10% on conventional heads which is to be enhanced on percentage basis in every three years and the enhancement should be at the rate of 10% in a span of three years.

So, the petitioner No.1(a) to 1(c), being the wife and children of deceased, are entitled for .48,400/- (each) towards loss of Spousal and Parental Consortium and also entitled for .18,150/- towards loss of estate and .18,150/- towards funeral expenses.

20. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent No.1 & 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Maxi cab bearing Regn.No.KA-51-AB-8488 by its driver.

The materials on record disclose that the offending vehicle was having valid and effective policy of insurance at the time of accident and the driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective licence to drive the vehicle.
So, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.

21. Issue No.3: In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of .25,56,238/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakh Fifty Six Thousand Two Hundred and Thirty Eight only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioner No.1(A) being the wife of deceased is entitled for 60%, and petitioner No.1(B) and 1(C) are minor daughters are entitled for 20% each of the compensation amount.

In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.1(A), 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1(A), and 40% of the amount shall be kept in FD in any Nationalized bank or Schedule Bank near to her place for a period of 3 years without encumbrance.
She is entitled for interest that accrues on F.D periodically.

20% each of compensation amount allotted to the share of minor petitioner No.1(B)
and 1(C) shall be kept in FD in their name of minor petitioners in any of the Nationalized Bank or Scheduled Bank of the choice of minor guardian for a period of 3 years or till they attains the age of majority whichever is later.

The statement of wife and relatives of deceased cannot be considered as sufficient proof to ascertain the cause of death.
The PM Report placed before the tribunal does not disclose the aspect of presence of traces of alcohol in the body.
In PM report, it clearly stated that the cause of death is due to infection of right leg, which is the injured part of the deceased.
The materials on record disclose that the deceased sustained injury to the leg and the PM report indicates the aspect of infection being caused to right leg which is got injured in the accident.
As such, as per the PM Report, the cause of death appears to be due to infection of right leg and not due to the reasons stated by wife and relatives of deceased in their statement before the police.
The report as per Ex.P13, is arrived after examination and analysis of parts of the body in accordance with scientific methods and said results prevail over the statement given by wife and relatives of deceased. Post mortem is the authenticated document for ascertaining the cause of death.

No materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to disprove or rebut the document furnished by petitioners related to age of deceased.
